name: Confirm dialog
purpose: Make the user pause before an action that is hard to undo or has significant consequences, and let them confirm or back out with certainty.
whenToUse: Permanently deleting data without an undo (delete project, remove member, empty trash).
Actions with large or external consequences (publish to the public, send to 500 people, revoke access).
Discarding unsaved work the user cannot recover (leave with unsaved changes).
Irreversible high-impact actions that deserve type-to-confirm (delete workspace, delete account).
whenNotToUse: Reversible actions. Do the action and offer Undo in a toast instead; a dialog for every delete trains users to click through.
Low-risk or frequent actions (archive, mark as read, remove from a list).
Asking for information or settings. That is a form dialog, not a confirmation.
Reporting results or errors. Use a toast or an inline message.
Stacking a confirmation on top of another confirmation.
anatomy: Backdrop: dims the page; clicking it cancels.
Title: a question with a specific verb and the object (Delete project "Atlas"?). Never Are you sure?
Body: one sentence of consequence (This permanently removes 24 files. This cannot be undone.).
Optional type-to-confirm field: label names the exact text to type; the confirm button stays disabled until it matches.
Footer: Cancel (secondary) and Confirm, right aligned; Confirm is last. Stacked full width on narrow screens.

variants.description: Cancel (secondary) and a primary verb button. Initial focus on Confirm.
variants.useWhen: Consequential but not destructive: archive, publish, transfer.

variants.description: Cancel and a SOLID destructive button (.btn-danger) with trash icon and explicit verb (Delete project). Initial focus on Cancel.
Destructive plus a field asking the user to type the object name; the destructive button is disabled until the text matches exactly. Initial focus on the field.
variants.useWhen: Irreversible, high-impact actions such as deleting a workspace or account.

behavior: Initial focus: Cancel for destructive dialogs (a stray Enter must not destroy anything), Confirm for non-destructive ones, the input for type-to-confirm.
Esc, backdrop click and Cancel all cancel and return focus to the element that opened the dialog.
Enter on the type-to-confirm field confirms only when the text matches.
Focus is trapped inside the dialog while open.
The confirm label repeats the verb of the title (Delete project), never OK or Yes.
While the action runs, the confirm button shows a spinner and ignores repeat clicks; the dialog closes on success. Errors appear inline in the dialog.
After confirming, do not add a success toast when the UI already shows the change.
accessibility: role=dialog (alertdialog for destructive confirmations) with aria-modal=true, aria-labelledby the title and aria-describedby the consequence sentence.
Focus moves into the dialog on open, is trapped, and returns to the trigger on close.
Never rely on colour alone: the destructive button has a verb and an icon, white text on --danger-solid reaches at least 4.5:1.
The type-to-confirm field has a visible label that names the exact text; the disabled state is conveyed with the disabled attribute, not only opacity.
Keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab cycle, Esc cancels, Enter activates the focused button.

The background page is inert while the dialog is open (focus, clicks and assistive technology are confined to the dialog). An alertdialog is not dismissed by clicking the backdrop; Esc and the Cancel button answer it. A plain dialog may be dismissed by backdrop click.
The consequence sentence is the accessible description (aria-describedby); in React pass it as the Dialog description prop.
